W3 / W11 (jcstress) and H1 (Lincheck): NodeCacheWithLRU and PtracksArray, Phase 2 cache campaign
===============================================================================================

Machine: Apple M5 Pro (AArch64, 18 cores), Temurin 21.0.12.1. jcstress 0.16, Lincheck 2.39 (coursier).
Every forked/Lincheck VM runs with -javaagent:entityagent.jar (CacheMC.<clinit> refuses to run without it),
-Doptimus.profile.enableXSFT=false, and the probe property's policy forced to NCPolicy.Basic (no proxies).

Commands (from probes/cache/modelcheck):
  ./fetch.sh                      # jcstress.cp, lincheck.cp (coursier)
  ./build.sh                      # scalac+javac ProbeDag.java/CacheFixtures.scala from probes/cache/src -> classes/fixtures;
                                  # src/common + src/jcstress -> classes/jcstress; src/common + src/lincheck -> classes/lincheck
  ./run.sh smoke                  # sequential sanity of the CacheMC helpers (put/get/collide/evict/resize/clear, C1 and L2)
  ./run.sh jcstress default 'optimus\.graph\.(cache\.W3|tracking\.ttracks\.W11).*' -v
  ./run.sh lincheck                                  # strict spec, hand-written scenarios first: fails with H1-A
  # final runs (results/lincheck-full-*.txt, lincheck-c1-1[12].txt), one JVM per seed, all in parallel:
  TAG=full-$i ./run.sh lincheck -Dmc.lax=clear,resize,ledger,sweep -Dmc.seed=$i -Dmc.iterations=10 -Dmc.invocations=3000 \
      -Dmc.handwritten=$([ $i = 1 ] && echo true || echo false)                       # i = 1..10
  TAG=c1-$i ./run.sh lincheck -Dmc.concurrency=1 -Dmc.lax=clear,resize,sweep -Dmc.seed=$i -Dmc.iterations=5 -Dmc.invocations=3000  # i = 11, 12
  ./run.sh shards N -Dname=X [-Dmc.*]                # same thing via the script (seeds 1..N, 100/N scenarios each)

Key fixtures: W3 keys are the P0 fixture TweakableLeaf (CacheMC.key, ProbeEntity(0), one int arg, attached to one
root); H1 keys are MCKey, a plain-Java PropertyNode with the same identity (Lincheck cannot walk the fixture's
record classes). Caches are real UNodeCache instances (unregistered from Caches.sharedCaches right after
construction): "C1" = new UNodeCache(name, 16) (concurrency 1, no ledgers, every touch takes updateLock); "L2" =
UNodeCache(name, 16, concurrency 2, batch 1, padding 1) (two ledgers that catch up on the second record).
Arbiters read presence with CacheMC.liveFor (walk of the current table, no touch) and LRU/table agreement with
CacheMC.desync (getSize() to flush ledgers, then LRU-not-table, table-not-LRU, size field minus live LRU length).

Verdict summary
---------------
W3 (a) A_SameKey              OK. 109 M samples, never two live nodes, lookup always returns the winner (W1 holds).
W3 (b) B_SameBucket[NonEmpty] OK. 193 M samples, no lost insert for colliding keys, empty or non-empty bucket.
W3 (c) C_PutVsClear C1/L2     OK. 118 M samples, no LRU/table desync, no size drift.
W3 (d) D_PutVsResize C1/L2    OPTIMUS-57931 observed as INTERESTING, as predicted: put vs setMaxSize(32) vs
                              setMaxSize(16) leaves the new key in the LRU but not in the table (lookup misses it
                              for good; size counts it) in 3,962 / 131.5 M (3.0e-5, C1) and 5,788 / 151.5 M
                              (3.8e-5, L2). The other direction (table-not-LRU) and loss of an existing key: never.
W3 (e) E_TouchVsEvict C1/L2   OK. The "hit, then evicted" case (lookup returns key 0 but the concurrent insert's
                              eviction still removes it) is 1.54% (C1) and 0.29% (L2). See note on the spec below.
W3 (f) F_PutClearVsHit C1/L2  Not reproduced by jcstress (62 M samples): the Lincheck-found inLedger race (H1-B)
                              needs the hitter preempted inside one synchronized block.
W11    LastSlotVsResize       FAILED, D12 confirmed on AArch64: 5 FORBIDDEN samples in 4.0 G over three default
                              runs (1 / 844 M, 1 / 719 M, 3 / 2.44 G uncontended): nextFree 9, capacity 16, one null
                              slot below nextFree, one caller missing (either actor's). Configurations: split
                              compilation C2/C1, C2/interpreter, interpreter/C2 (C2 scheduling randomisers on) and
                              interpreter/C1 without randomisers, so not a stress-flag artefact.
H1 Lincheck                   Strict memo spec FAILS, three distinct ways, all with traces: H1-A put lost into
                              a retired table (OPTIMUS-57931), H1-B (new) an entry inserted by a completed put
                              survives a later clear() through the inLedger shortcut (concurrency > 1 only), H1-C
                              clear() is a non-atomic sweep. With those three documented as relaxations, PASSED:
                              L2 312 000 executions (104 scenarios x 3 000 interleavings, 10 JVMs), C1 42 000
                              (14 x 3 000). Never two live nodes for a key outside a setMaxSize window, never a
                              miss on a live key outside one, and LRU/table always agree except H1-A.
                              Budget: 3 000 invocations per scenario, not the requested 10 000 (eager Lincheck
                              instrumentation runs ~10-25 executions/s per JVM; 100 x 10 000 would be ~10 h).

New findings
------------
H1-A (known, OPTIMUS-57931, now with a 2-actor trace) put vs setMaxSize: putIfAbsent reads `table` once and
retries its CAS on that array; if setMaxSize swaps the table and finishes both moveEntries passes in between, the
CAS succeeds on the retired array. The entry reaches the LRU (newEntryAdded) but no table: size counts it, every
later lookup misses it, a concurrent put of the same key inserts a second node, and threads still holding the old
array can hit it until they reload. Lincheck minimised it to init [put 0, put 1], par [put 2 | setMaxSize(32)]
(results/lincheck-strict-custom.txt, validate: LRU-not-table=1). jcstress W3 (d): 3.0e-5 (C1) / 3.8e-5 (L2).

H1-B (new, M) the inLedger shortcut lets an entry escape clear() (cacheConcurrency > 1 only).
NodeCacheWithLRU.touchEntry(Ledger, entry): `if (entry.inLedger) return;` then, inside synchronized(l),
`entry.inLedger = true` before `l.records[l.count++] = entry`. clear() -> catchupCore() peeks `if (l.count == 0)
continue;` without the lock. Interleaving (results/lincheck-lax-3.txt, condensed):
  T1 putIfAbsent(6): CAS NCEntryV#2 into the bucket                      [NodeCacheBase.java:133]  -- switch
  T2 putIfAbsent(6): finds NCEntryV#2 (hit), touchEntry(Ledger#3):
       inLedger ➜ false; MONITORENTER; inLedger = true; count ➜ 0          [NodeCacheWithLRU.java:215-225] -- switch
  T1 newEntryAdded -> touchEntry: inLedger is true -> return (no record); putIfAbsent returns 1096
  T3 clear(): catchupCore skips Ledger#3 (count 0), LRU walk does not contain NCEntryV#2
  T3 getIfPresent(6): 96   <- node inserted by a put that returned before clear() started
  T2 records[0] = NCEntryV#2; the entry reaches the LRU on the next catch-up
So a node that was in the cache, visible, and inserted by a completed put survives a clear() that starts after
that put returned (clear(CauseUntrackedTweakableTweaked) etc. rely on clear meaning "nothing from before"). The
entry is also invisible to eviction and size until the hitter's append lands. Window: one hitter between two
stores inside its synchronized block, plus a full clear. jcstress W3 (f) did not reproduce it in 31 M samples
(L2); Lincheck found it from random scenarios in 2 of 10 seeds (lax=clear,resize run: seeds 3 and 4).
Fix options: have the inserter always append its own record (drop the inLedger early return for new entries,
i.e. before == null), or make catchupCore take each ledger's lock instead of peeking count.

H1-C (new, L, by design but undocumented) clear() is not atomic: it removes LRU entries one at a time under
updateLock while lookups are lock-free, so a reader sees a partially cleared cache (key 3 already gone, key 4
still present, both inserted before the clear: results/lincheck-c1-12-partialclear.txt, concurrency 1). Matters
only if a caller expects clear() to be a cut (H1-B makes it weaker still).

H1-D (known, at-least-once by design) while setMaxSize runs, lookups miss and puts insert a second node for a live
key; after the move both duplicates stay in the table (moveEntries reverses bucket order, so a later lookup may
return either). Accepted by the spec inside the setMaxSize interval.

Also confirmed: an insert in flight across clear() survives it (put CASes into the table, clear runs, put then
records it): the clearing thread itself sees the node before and after its clear (results/lincheck-resize-only.txt,
hand-written scenario 3). This is linearizable if put is placed after clear, except when another thread observed
the node before clear started, which is the case in that trace.

W3 (e) note: the brief's "stale hit then miss" is reachable under sequential consistency (walk reads value, the
insert's eviction removes it, catchupEntry sees removed() and returns), so it is ACCEPTABLE_INTERESTING, not
FORBIDDEN: it is the approximate-LRU case (a touch lost to a concurrent eviction), indistinguishable from an R16
stale read of NCEntry.value. Rates 1.54% (C1), 0.29% (L2). L2 needed two inserts in actor 2: a single insert only
lands in a ledger and never evicts before the arbiter (first run: 100% "hit; no eviction yet").

W11 note: the FORBIDDEN samples are exactly ring 4b S9 / D12: nextFree 9 with a null at slot 7 and one of the two
callers missing, so every caller at or after the gap is invisible to the traversals (I6). Rate ~1 per 0.8 G
samples; seen with each actor in the interpreter, C1 or C2. Fix as in S9: make nextFree volatile or re-read the
copied tail with getVolatile before the data CAS.

H1 Lincheck (model checking)
---------------------------
Spec (MemoVerifier, nondeterministic, searched over all linearizations consistent with Lincheck's HB clocks):
per key the set of live nodes; putIfAbsent returns a live node or inserts its own only if none is live;
getIfPresent returns a live node and misses only if none is live; clear empties; setMaxSize is an interval
[begin, end] inside which a miss or a second insert is allowed (at-least-once window); eviction only once more
than maxSize entries were inserted since the last clear (never, in practice, with 8 keys). @Validate after the
post part: LRU and table agree (desync 0,0,0). Relaxations, each one a documented deviation above:
  lax=resize  put inside a setMaxSize may be lost (H1-A): ghost node, hittable until the resize ends; validate
              tolerates LRU-not-table.
  lax=clear   put = insert then LRU record; clear spares entries not yet recorded (in-flight insert).
  lax=ledger  a hit pins the entry until it returns; clear spares pinned entries (H1-B).
  lax=sweep   clear = interval; entries it will remove are fixed at begin and may vanish one by one (H1-C).
Weaknesses: the at-least-once window is the whole setMaxSize call; lax=ledger lets any concurrent hit protect an
entry, wider than the real two-store window; eviction is "anything goes" once over capacity (not reached);
a duplicate allowed in the window is never checked for being the one a later lookup returns.

Testability: Lincheck 2.39's default lazy instrumentation walks the object graph from the test instance and its
statics and dies on record classes ("can't get field offset on a record class": ProbeDag.Key via the fixture keys,
then SecureClassLoader$CodeSourceKey via something reachable from the cache). -Dlincheck.instrumentAllClasses=true
(eager) works, gives full traces, and is what run.sh uses; the cost is ~10 executions/s per JVM. Lincheck 3.7 has no
@StateRepresentation and NPEs in SnapshotTracker.restoreValues on this code base. Lincheck's own scenario generator
is seeded identically in every JVM, so H1CacheLincheck generates scenarios itself from -Dmc.seed (uniform over the
4 operations, keys 0..7, sizes 16|32, 4 before / 3x3 parallel / 3 after) and passes them as custom scenarios, which
lets 10 JVMs share the budget. NodeTask still cannot be instrumented (TPDMask fields), irrelevant here: the keys are
passive and every shared access is in NodeCacheBase / NodeCacheWithLRU / NCEntry, which the traces show
instrumented (the entity agent does not rewrite them).

Lincheck runs (results/lincheck-*.txt)
--------------------------------------
Strict spec (no relaxation), hand-written scenarios first: FAILS on the first one (H1-A), results/lincheck-strict-custom.txt.
lax=resize only: FAILS on hand-written scenario 3 (insert in flight observed across clear), results/lincheck-resize-only.txt.
lax=clear,resize, 10 JVMs x 10 generated scenarios x 10 000 (results/lincheck-lax-*.txt; the 5 still running
  were stopped when the spec changed): FAILED seeds 1 (ghost hit on a lost insert, before ghosts were modelled),
  3 and 4 (H1-B), 6 (H1-C), 8 (not analysed; its scenario passes under the final spec).
concurrency 1, lax=clear,resize: FAILED seed 12 (H1-C), results/lincheck-c1-12-partialclear.txt.
Final spec, mc.invocations=3000:
  lincheck-c1-11.txt: PASSED 27000 executions verified, 260 needed the setMaxSize at-least-once window, 62 only linearize with a lax relaxation; 1299.6s 
  lincheck-c1-12.txt: PASSED 15000 executions verified, 285 needed the setMaxSize at-least-once window, 124 only linearize with a lax relaxation; 823.3s
